subject: Python kernel dies when accessing fitted Stan Model.

messages.author: 9860719641632b58
messages.subject: Python kernel dies when accessing fitted Stan Model.
parts:
I am not sure whether this is a stan problem at all.
I am using pystan. I can run my stan model as usual, but as soon as I call it I get an error message, as follows.

>>> fittedModel = model.sampling ( data = ..., ...)

>>> fittedModel

/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/numpy/core/_methods.py:59: RuntimeWarning: Mean of empty slice.
  warnings.warn("Mean of empty slice.", RuntimeWarning)
/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/numpy/core/_methods.py:83: RuntimeWarning: Degrees of freedom <= 0 for slice
  warnings.warn("Degrees of freedom <= 0 for slice", RuntimeWarning)
Exception TypeError: "'float' object cannot be interpreted as an index" in 'pystan._chains.get_kept_samples' ignored
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::domain_error'
  what():  Error in function mean(d): v(St6vectorIdSaIdEE) has size 0, but must have a non-zero size

I only get this error message, if I do it exactly as above. When I try to access my model by doing something like 
>>> fittedModel.extract()
my python kernel dies. 

This happens with all my models that used to work fine before and on two different computers, running Ubuntu/Mint.
I am not entirely sure about packages I updated on both computers, other than the latest version of stan (2.4.0.3) and cython (0.21)

A maybe related issue: I've been using stan for about 4 weeks and it runs unstable in IPython. Especially Ipython notebook sometimes crashes, after
I did sampling in stan. I therefore switched to plain python.


Thank you!
